pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is the key question of this lesson? (1 mark)
   A. What is the price of food?
   B. Who is the tallest pupil?
   C. How should we respond to instructions?
   D. How far is the market?

2. How should you find out how your mother tongue forms plurals? (1 mark)
   A. Guess from English
   B. Add s to every word
   C. Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   D. Ignore it

3. Plural means (1 mark)
   A. more than one
   B. nothing
   C. only one
   D. the biggest

4. Which of these is NOT a way of building vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. Keeping a word bank
   B. Using a dictionary
   C. Making flashcards
   D. Never looking at new words

5. Which of these is a cultural food word? (1 mark)
   A. window
   B. pencil
   C. porridge
   D. ruler

6. Which letter hangs below the base line in English handwriting? (1 mark)
   A. o
   B. c
   C. a
   D. g

7. What should you do if you make a mistake in your exercise book? (1 mark)
   A. Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   B. Tear the page
   C. Scribble over it hard
   D. Blame a friend

8. What should you do first when you give an instruction to a friend? (1 mark)
   A. Plan the steps in order
   B. Say all steps at once quickly
   C. Shout
   D. Walk away

9. Which of these is an instruction? (1 mark)
   A. The door was open.
   B. Close the door.
   C. A door has a handle.
   D. The door is red.

10. Which is a mistake in reading aloud? (1 mark)
   A. Practising first
   B. Pausing at full stops
   C. Looking up at the audience
   D. Reading too fast so nobody can follow

11. How can recording your reading help you? (1 mark)
   A. You can listen back and see how to improve
   B. It makes you forget
   C. It deletes the story
   D. It ends practice

12. Which sentence should be read with a rising voice in English? (1 mark)
   A. We go to school.
   B. Are you coming to school?
   C. Come to school.
   D. You are coming to school.

13. What does a full stop show? (1 mark)
   A. A list of items
   B. A sudden feeling
   C. A question
   D. The end of a statement

14. Which sentence ends correctly? (1 mark)
   A. The sun is hot,
   B. The sun is hot.
   C. The sun is hot:
   D. The sun is hot?

15. What is the first thing to do when someone gets a burn? (1 mark)
   A. Ignore it
   B. Put the burn under cool running water
   C. Rub it hard
   D. Cover it with dirt

16. In grammar, a verb is a word that (1 mark)
   A. names a person
   B. shows an action
   C. names a place
   D. joins two sentences

17. What is the best way to read your part in a dialogue? (1 mark)
   A. Read other people's lines
   B. Never practise
   C. Read it very quickly
   D. Practise your lines with the right feeling

18. In The road was congested and the matatu could not move, what does congested mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very short
   B. Very wide
   C. Very crowded
   D. Very clean

19. Which word shows the first step? (1 mark)
   A. Lastly
   B. Finally
   C. In the end
   D. First

20. What is the best way to check the order of your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Cover it
   B. Fold the page
   C. Copy it
   D. Read it aloud

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

22. Describe how a newsreader should read a weather bulletin. (4 marks)

23. Plan a reader's theatre for a short passage about rain. Say who the roles are, how to practise and how the audience gives feedback. (5 marks)

24. Give the plural of each English noun: cabbage, onion. (2 marks)

25. Explain what to do when you get a small burn and why. (4 marks)

26. Explain why clear instructions are important when it rains. (3 marks)

27. State two uses of a full stop and a capital letter in a sentence. (2 marks)

28. State three steps for reading your part in a dialogue. (3 marks)

29. Write one instruction from the road safety dialogue. (2 marks)

30. Name four question words used to check comprehension. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #7 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — How should we respond to instructions?
   The lesson asks how we should respond to instructions in songs and games.

2. C — Ask an elder, a parent or the teacher
   Languages form plurals in different ways, so we ask people who know the language well.

3. A — more than one
   Plural nouns name two or more.

4. D — Never looking at new words
   Ignoring new words does not build vocabulary.

5. C — porridge
   Porridge is a food. The others are not.

6. D — g
   The letter g has a tail that goes below the line.

7. A — Rub it out gently or draw one neat line through it
   Neat correction keeps the page clean.

8. A — Plan the steps in order
   Planning helps to give clear instructions.

9. B — Close the door.
   Close the door tells you what to do.

10. D — Reading too fast so nobody can follow
   Speed that is too fast loses meaning.

11. A — You can listen back and see how to improve
   Playing back shows where to improve.

12. B — Are you coming to school?
   It is a question.

13. D — The end of a statement
   A full stop ends a statement.

14. B — The sun is hot.
   A statement ends with a full stop.

15. B — Put the burn under cool running water
   Cool water reduces pain and damage.

16. B — shows an action
   Verbs show actions.

17. D — Practise your lines with the right feeling
   Practice with expression helps fluency.

18. C — Very crowded
   The matatu could not move because there was too much traffic.

19. D — First
   First begins the sequence.

20. D — Read it aloud
   Reading aloud shows if the order makes sense.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

22. (4 marks)
   Answer: Speak clearly, keep a steady pace, use a friendly and confident tone, pause at full stops and look at the audience.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct points.

23. (5 marks)
   Answer: Roles such as narrator, farmer, child and rain. Read your part silently three times, mark stressed words, then read aloud with expression. The audience gives one good point and one improvement.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for suitable roles, two marks for practice steps and one mark for feedback.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: cabbages, onions
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct plural.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put it under cool running water for several minutes to reduce pain, cover it with a clean cloth and tell an adult or go to a clinic.
   Working / marking points: One mark each for cool water, the reason, clean cover and telling an adult.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Clear instructions tell people what to do to stay safe and dry, so they do not make mistakes or get hurt.
   Working / marking points: One mark for staying safe, one for avoiding mistakes, one for a clear link to rain.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: A capital letter begins a sentence and a full stop ends it.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct use.

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read silently first, underline your lines, practise them, watch the punctuation, wait for your cue.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: Look right, then left, then right again. (or Cross at a zebra crossing.)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a correct instruction and one for a complete sentence.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: Who, what, where, when, why, how (any four).
   Working / marking points: One mark for two correct question words and two marks for four.
